experiment: Phase 5 - simulated quantization vs SAE feature interpretability

config.quantization_method: uniform min-max weight rounding (simulated, not a production backend)
config.note: Held out from SAE training data, which used train[:3000]

metrics_defined.recall_at_5: Fraction of baseline top-5 activating token positions retained in the quantized variant's top-5, counting only positive-activation matches
metrics_defined.mean_correlation: Mean per-feature Pearson correlation between baseline and quantized activations, streaming-computed across all 500 held-out documents
metrics_defined.perplexity_ratio: Quantized-variant perplexity divided by baseline perplexity on the same held-out set
metrics_defined.top1_agreement: Fraction of next-token predictions identical between baseline and quantized variant

finding: Under naive uniform weight rounding, behavioral quality (perplexity, top-1 agreement) and SAE feature interpretability (recall@5, correlation) degrade together, not independently. 16-bit is a clean negative control. 4-bit destroys the model outright rather than revealing a subtle interpretability-specific danger.
limitations: Simulated quantization (uniform min-max weight rounding), not a production backend such as GPTQ/AWQ
Single model, single layer, single SAE training seed
No behavior-preserving quantization configuration was found or tested
